# Adjudication Task — Chapter 419

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃419화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|이정룡은 문득 생각했다.
  6|
  7|‘어디서부터, 무엇이 잘못되었을까.’
  8|
  9|형님의 핏줄을 몰아내고 아레스 길드를 장악한 것?
 10|
 11|각종 불법을 저질러 끊임없이 길드를 성장시키고, 그러고도 만족하는 법 없이 욕심을 채워 나간 것?
 12|
 13|그것도 아니라면…….
 14|
 15|‘저 녀석과 적이 된 것?’
 16|
 17|이정룡의 시선이 한 사람에게 닿았다. 출혈로 인해 전신 곳곳이 피로 물들어 있는 청년.
 18|
 19|하늘을 바라보며 크게 심호흡한 그가 입술을 뗐다.
 20|
 21|“정룡아.”
 22|
 23|어째서일까. 그 나직한 목소리를 듣는 순간 이정룡은 등골이 서늘해졌다. 상처 하나 입지 않았음에도 날붙이에 베인 기분이다.
 24|
 25|그런 그를 바라보는 청년, 진태경의 입가에 광포한 웃음이 맺혔다.
 26|
 27|“발톱 자르자.”
 28|
 29|“……!”
 30|
 31|파팟!
 32|
 33|바람이 불고, 두 사람 사이에 존재하던 공간이 사라진 그 순간. 이정룡은 파공성과 함께 검을 휘둘렀다.
 34|
 35|쉬익!
 36|
 37|눈부신 기의 집약체가 진태경의 몸뚱어리를 갈랐다. 하지만 뿜어져 나와야 할 핏물 대신 바람이 흩어졌다.
 38|
 39|실체가 아닌 잔상(殘像). 이정룡의 머릿속에서 붉은색 경종이 울렸다.
 40|
 41|‘뒤!’
 42|
 43|검을 휘두르기에는 너무 늦었다. 이정룡은 번개처럼 돌아서며 주먹을 내질렀다. 새하얀 오러에 휩싸인 주먹과, 푸른 화염이 실린 손바닥이 부딪쳤다.
 44|
 45|꽈앙!
 46|
 47|세상이 뒤흔들렸다. 아니, 흔들린 것은 이정룡의 시야였다.
 48|
 49|항거할 수 없는 힘에 튕겨 나간 그가 허공에서 몸을 뒤집으며 신형을 바로잡았다.
 50|
 51|주먹이 시큰거리고 속에서 무언가가 울컥 솟구쳤다. 하지만 핏물을 뱉어 낼 틈조차 주어지지 않았다.
 52|
 53|쐐애애액!
 54|
 55|어느새 코앞까지 들이닥친 창날. 진태경이 쏘아 보낸 창이 이정룡의 가슴을 노렸다. 이를 악문 그가 온 힘을 불어넣어 검을 쳐올렸다.
 56|
 57|카가가가각! 쾅!
 58|
 59|아슬아슬하게 빗나간 창이 콘크리트를 부수며 거대한 크레이터를 남겼다.
 60|
 61|창을 흘리는 데에는 성공했지만, 가공할 만한 힘과 회전력에 찢어진 손아귀에서는 피가 튀었다.
 62|
 63|하지만 이정룡은 개의치 않고 자욱한 먼지구름 너머로 발을 뻗었다.
 64|
 65|퍼엉-!
 66|
 67|쾌속한 속도를 이기지 못한 먼지와 안개가 뿔뿔이 흩어졌다. 이정룡이 내디딘 걸음의 끝엔, 한 사람이 있었다.
 68|
 69|“저돌적인데? 내 취향이야.”
 70|
 71|어느새 새로운 창을 든 진태경이 종횡으로 창날을 내리그었다. 공간이 갈라지고 화염이 솟구쳤다. 이정룡이 내지른 검 끝은 그 중심을 정확히 꿰뚫었다.
 72|
 73|후웅, 펑!
 74|
 75|압축된 공기가 터져 나갔다. 화염이 갈라지고 새로운 길이 열렸다. 화살처럼 쏘아진 이정룡의 신형이 진태경을 향해 달려들었다.
 76|
 77|‘죽어라.’
 78|
 79|오직 한 가지 일념(一念)을 담은 검은 휘황하게 빛났고, 빛처럼 빨랐다.
 80|
 81|그러나 느려진 세상 속에서 바라본 진태경의 눈은 분명 웃고 있었다.
 82|
 83|‘이건…….’
 84|
 85|무엇인가 잘못됐다.
 86|
 87|이정룡의 생각이 미처 이어지기도 전에, 창을 쥔 진태경의 손이 흐릿해졌다.
 88|
 89|동시에 당장이라도 그의 목젖을 파고들 것 같던 검신을 후려치는 거대한 힘이 있었다.
 90|
 91|쉭! 꽈앙!
 92|
 93|귓가가 먹먹해질 만한 굉음이 울려 퍼졌다. 자의와는 상관없이 십여 미터를 미끄러진 이정룡은 치밀어 오르는 핏물을 삼켰다.
 94|
 95|‘아직 끝나지 않았다.’
 96|
 97|쓰러져서도, 약한 모습을 보여서도 안 된다. 그는 이정룡이다. 인류 역사상 어느 때보다 격렬했던 대격변이라는 소용돌이를 헤쳐 나온 장본인이자, 시대가 낳은 한 사람의 효웅(梟雄).
 98|
 99|이정룡은 거미줄 같은 실금이 간 검을 움켜쥐었다.
100|
101|‘죽지 않는다. 죽을 수 없다.’
102|
103|이 자리에 오르기까지 많은 우여곡절이 있었다. 아득한 절망도 겪었고, 참을 수 없이 분노한 날도 있었다.
104|
105|누군가의 그림자에 가려져, 이인자라는 이름으로 반평생을 살았다.
106|
107|아니, 어쩌면 지금조차도.
108|
109|하지만…….
110|
111|“더 이상은 아니다.”
112|
113|투둑. 투두두둑.
114|
115|전신의 혈관이 도드라지고 근육이 부풀었다. 이정룡의 전신에서 일어난 강대한 기운이 사방을 짓눌렀다.
116|
117|최후의 최후를 위해 남겨 둔 마지막 힘까지 모조리 끌어올린 그는 핏발 선 눈으로 진태경을 노려보았다.
118|
119|“그는 이제 존재하지 않는 사람이나 다름없다. 세계 최고는…… 바로 나다.”
120|
121|우우우웅.
122|
123|이정룡을 둘러싼 모든 것이 부르르 떨렸다. 그런 그를 바라보는 진태경의 눈빛은 일말의 흔들림 없이 차분했다.
124|
125|“글쎄, 내 생각에는 아닐 것 같은데.”
126|
127|콰아아아!
128|
129|두 사람의 전신에서 흘러나온 기파가 사방을 할퀴었다.
130|
131|찰나를 쪼개고 쪼갠 짧은 순간 속, 그들은 동시에 서로를 향해 달려들었다.
132|
133|
134|
135|* * *
136|
137|
138|
139|꽈앙!
140|
141|격돌은 섬광과도 같았고, 여파는 거대했다. 세상을 뒤흔드는 굉음 속에서 그들은 두 줄기의 바람이 되어 뒤섞였다.
142|
143|푸른 화염을 머금은 창날과 눈부시도록 밝은 빛에 휩싸인 검이 서로를 향해 날아들었다.
144|
145|쉬쉬쉬쉬쉭!
146|
147|공간을 격하며 달려드는 빛무리.
148|
149|지면을 박차며 솟구친 진태경이 엄청난 기세로 창을 내리꽂았다. 일 격, 이 격, 삼 격. 검을 부딪쳐 갈 때마다 굉음과 함께 엄청난 충격파가 터져 나왔다.
150|
151|어느새 이정룡의 입가에서 흘러나온 핏물이 점점이 흩뿌려졌다.
152|
153|“쿨럭.”
154|
155|순간 휘청이는 신형. 늙은 사자가 찰나 보인 약한 모습에 젊은 숫사자가 이빨을 들이민다.
156|
157|횡으로 휘둘려진 창날이 이정룡의 옆구리를 힘차게 베어 왔다.
158|
159|쾅!
160|
161|지진이라도 난 것처럼 땅이 흔들렸다.
162|
163|서로의 숨이 닿을 만큼 가까운 거리, 가까스로 창을 막아낸 이정룡은 맞댄 무기 사이로 화염을 쏟아 내고 있는 한 쌍의 눈동자와 시선이 마주쳤다.
164|
165|‘젊구나. 과거의 내가 그랬던 것처럼.’
166|
167|어째서였을까. 하필이면 이런 상황에서 문득 그런 생각이 든 이유는.
168|
169|보잘것없고 초라했던 자신의 옛 모습을 떠올리느라, 화염에 휩싸여 날아드는 진태경의 손바닥을 막지 못한 것은.
170|
171|퍼엉-!
172|
173|뜨겁다. 전신을 빈틈없이 보호하고 있던 기운이 깨져 나가고 끔찍한 열기가 폐부로 스며든다.
174|
175|눈앞을 물들이는 푸른 화염과 고통 속에서, 이정룡의 뇌리에 오래전의 기억들이 쏜살같이 스쳐 지나갔다.
176|
177|
178|
179|‘이름이?’
180|
181|‘예?’
182|
183|‘아, 그쪽한테 물은 거 맞아요.’
184|
185|‘갑자기 웬 통성명입니까?’
186|
187|
188|
189|대격변 초기. 수많은 몬스터에 포위된 절체절명의 상황에서 만난 한 사람.
190|
191|
192|
193|‘그냥. 내 또래로 보이길래. 반가워서.’
194|
195|‘젊은 친구가 갑자기 말이 짧아지시네. 나보다 한참 어려 보이는데.’
196|
197|‘그럼 친구 할까요. 난 상관없는데.’
198|
199|‘……이런 상황에서 그런 말이 나옵니까?’
200|
201|‘좀 그런가.’
202|
203|
204|
205|죽음에 대한 공포로 반쯤 미쳐 버린 놈이라고 생각했다.
206|
207|그 미친놈이 홀연히 앞으로 나서 수천 마리가 넘는 몬스터를 휩쓸어 버리기 전까지는.
208|
209|콰드드득!
210|
211|
212|
213|‘이런 미친…….’
214|
215|‘이때다! 돌격-!’
216|
217|
218|
219|전투가 끝난 후, 그가 다시 찾아와 던진 물음은 처음과 같았다.
220|
221|
222|
223|‘이름이?’
224|
225|‘이정룡……입니다.’
226|
227|‘이름 멋있다. 그럼 나이는? 오. 내가 다섯 살 많네. 얼마 차이도 안 나는데 그냥 친구 할까요?’
228|
229|‘아닙니다. 형님.’
230|
231|
232|
233|그는 빌어먹을 정도로 동안이었고, 믿을 수 없을 만큼 강했다.
234|
235|A급 헌터 이정룡은 그와의 첫 만남에서 자신의 영웅을, 동시에 넘을 수 없는 거대한 산맥을 발견했다.
236|
237|
238|
239|‘그런데, 형님.’
240|
241|‘응?’
242|
243|‘혹시 성함이…….’
244|
245|‘아, 내가 아직 말을 안 해 줬구나.’
246|
247|
248|
249|그는 씩 웃으며 말했었다.
250|
251|
252|
253|‘천태민.’
254|
255|
256|
257|천태민. 천태민. 천태민…….
258|
259|몇 번을 되뇌어도 큰 울림을 남기는 한 사람의 이름. 잊으려 해도 뇌리에 각인 된 얼굴.
260|
261|이정룡의 인생에 거대한 그림자를 드리운 거인.
262|
263|“꺼져! 당장 내 앞에서 사라지란 말이다-!”
264|
265|이정룡은 끓어오르는 음성으로 부르짖었다. 고통으로 새하얗게 물들었던 시야가 유리처럼 깨어져 나가고 귓가를 스치는 바람이 맹렬하다.
266|
267|정신을 차린 다음 순간, 이정룡은 엄청난 충격과 함께 고층빌딩을 뚫고 차가운 콘크리트에 처박혔다.
268|
269|콰과광!
270|
271|“쿨럭.”
272|
273|입술 사이로 튀어나온 검붉은 핏물.
274|
275|시야는 흐릿했고 사지 곳곳에서 고통이 엄습했다. 모조리 부서진 갈비뼈가 내장을 건드렸는지 호흡이 힘겨웠으며, 부러진 왼팔과 다리는 힘없이 덜렁거렸다.
276|
277|‘포션, 포션을…….’
278|
279|마지막 기회다. 잠시라도 공격이 멈춘 이때 상처를 치료해야 한다.
280|
281|이정룡은 그나마 성한 오른팔로 옆구리를 더듬었지만, 아공간 주머니가 있어야 할 그곳은 텅 비어 있었다.
282|
283|대신 그가 발견한 것은 저 멀리 자신을 향해 다가오는 한 사람이었다.
284|
285|“아, 혹시 이거 찾냐?”
286|
287|데구르르르. 툭.
288|
289|마법으로 강화된 유리병 하나가 굴러와 이정룡의 발치에 닿았다.
290|
291|숨만 붙어 있다면 누구든 살려 낸다는 기적의 물약, 바로 최상급 포션이었다.
292|
293|다만 그가 기억하는 마지막 상태와는 상당한 차이가 있었지만.
294|
295|“하도 목이 말라서 마셨는데 진짜 시원하더라. 약수터 어디 다녀?”
296|
297|천연덕스럽게 말하며 다가오는 그의 모습에, 이정룡은 헛웃음을 흘렸다.
298|
299|‘진태경.’
300|
301|이름, 얼굴, 성격. 모든 것이 다르다.
302|
303|하지만 지금 이 순간, 이정룡은 마침내 깨달을 수 있었다.
304|
305|진태경을 처음 마주했던 그 날, 가슴 깊숙한 곳에서 느꼈던 불안감과 흥미라는 두 글자로 포장하여 애써 외면했던 익숙함을.
306|
307|“정룡아.”
308|
309|귓가를 파고드는 나직한 목소리.
310|
311|어느새 코앞으로 다가온 진태경의 얼굴 위로 겹쳐지는 한 사람의 모습.
312|
313|이정룡은 신음처럼 중얼거렸다.
314|
315|“너는, 넌 도대체 누구냐.”
316|
317|묻고 싶었다. 미치도록 궁금했다.
318|
319|어찌하여 이렇게까지 그를 닮을 수 있는지.
320|
321|그를 따라 무수한 업적을 세우며 영웅이라 추앙받는 자신이 아니라, 저런 F급 헌터 따위가 더 강해질 수 있었는지!
322|
323|“나?”
324|
325|다음 순간, 입가에 미소를 띤 진태경이 말을 이었다.
326|

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;

“Cough.”

Why?

Heat.

[P102]

[P103]
“Your name?”

[P104]
“Pardon?”

“Ah, yes. I meant you.”

[P106]
“Why are you suddenly asking my name?”

[P107]
“Just because. You look about my age. Nice to meet someone my age.”

[P108]
“Young fellow, you’ve suddenly gotten awfully casual. You look much younger than me.”

[P109]
“Then should we be friends? I don’t mind.”

[P110]
“…Do you really have time to say things like that in a situation like this?”

[P111]
“Maybe not.”

[P112]
It was the early days of the Great Cataclysm. They had met while surrounded by countless monsters, trapped in a desperate life-or-death crisis.

[P113]
Lee Jungryong had thought the man was half-mad with fear of death.

[P114]
At least until that madman stepped forward and swept away more than a thousand monsters.

[P115]
*Crack-crack-crack!*

[P116]
“What the hell…?”

[P117]
“Now! Charge!”

[P118]
After the battle, the man returned and asked him the same question.

[P119]
“Your name?”

[P120]
“I’m Lee Jungryong…”

[P121]
“Cool name. How old are you? Oh, I’m five years older. That’s hardly a difference. Should we just be friends?”

[P122]
“No. Hyung.”

[P123]
He looked absurdly young and was unbelievably strong.

[P124]
At their first meeting, A-rank Hunter Lee Jungryong had found his hero—and, at the same time, an immense mountain range he could never cross.

[P125]
“By the way, hyung.”

[P126]
“Yeah?”

[P127]
“What’s your name…?”

[P128]
“Oh, I haven’t told you yet.”

[P129]
The man had grinned.

[P130]
“Cheon Taemin.”

[P131]
Cheon Taemin. Cheon Taemin. Cheon Taemin…

[P132]
No matter how many times he repeated the name, it resonated deeply within him.

[P133]
Even when he tried to forget, the face remained etched in his mind.

[P134]
A giant who cast an immense shadow over Lee Jungryong’s life.

[P135]
“Get lost! I said get out of my sight right now—!”

[P136]
Lee Jungryong roared, his voice boiling with rage.

[P137]
His vision, bleached white with pain, shattered like glass. The wind screamed past his ears.

[P138]
When he came to his senses, he was crashing through a high-rise building and slamming into cold concrete with tremendous force.

[P139]
*Kwa-gwa-gwang!*

[P140]
“Cough.”

[P141]
Dark-red blood spurted between his lips.

[P142]
His vision blurred, and pain assailed him from every part of his body.

[P143]
His shattered ribs must have been digging into his organs, because every breath was a struggle. His broken left arm and leg dangled uselessly.

[P144]
*A potion. The potion…*

[P145]
This was his last chance.

[P146]
The attack had stopped, if only for a moment. He had to heal himself now.

[P147]
Lee Jungryong groped at his side with his relatively uninjured right arm, but the spot where his dimensional pouch should have been was empty.

[P148]
Instead, he found someone approaching from far away.

[P149]
“Ah, looking for this?”

[P150]
*Rrrrrroll. Clink.*

[P151]
A magic-enhanced glass bottle rolled over and came to rest at Lee Jungryong’s feet.

[P152]
It was a top-tier potion, a miraculous medicine said to save anyone as long as they still drew breath.

[P153]
It looked considerably different from the last time Lee Jungryong had seen it.

[P154]
“I was so thirsty, I drank it. Man, that hit the spot. What mineral spring did you get it from?”

[P155]
As Jin Taekyung approached, speaking as casually as ever, Lee Jungryong let out a hollow laugh.

[P156]
*Jin Taekyung.*

[P157]
His name, face, and personality were all different.

[P158]
But at that moment, Lee Jungryong finally understood.

[P159]
When he had first encountered Jin Taekyung, he had felt something familiar deep in his chest. He had tried to ignore it, disguising it beneath the words *anxiety* and *interest*.

[P160]
“Jungryong.”

[P161]
The quiet voice pierced his ears.

[P162]
Jin Taekyung was already standing before him, the image of another person superimposed over his face.

[P163]
Lee Jungryong groaned out the words.

[P164]
“Who are you? Who the hell are you?”

[P165]
He wanted to ask. He was desperate to know.

[P166]
How could Jin Taekyung resemble him so closely?

[P167]
Why had some lowly F-rank Hunter grown stronger instead of Lee Jungryong—the man who had followed Cheon Taemin, accomplished countless feats, and been hailed as a hero?

[P168]
“Me?”

[P169]
Jin Taekyung smiled.

[P170]
“Your personal bully.”

[P171]

[P172]
“Brothers. Sworn brothers.”

[P173]
The two men had spoken different words with different meanings, yet both were smiling.

[P174]
Lee Jungryong stared blankly at those goddamn similar smiles, then slowly—very slowly—opened his mouth.

[P175]
“I…”

[P176]
Decades of his life and countless emotions rose and faded.

[P177]
The wait lasted no more than an instant, yet felt like eternity. At last, a hollow voice slipped between his lips.

[P178]
“I don’t regret it. Never.”

[P179]
If someone asked whether he truly had not even a handful of regrets, the answer was no.

[P180]
But Lee Jungryong could not regret it. He did not want to.

[P181]
He simply believed this was the ending that suited him best.

[P182]
“Kill me.”

[P183]
A cold reply fell upon Lee Jungryong’s bright smile.

[P184]
“Last words duly noted.”

[P185]
*Fwoom.*

[P186]
The spearhead that followed burned with blue flame.

[P187]
* * *

[P188]
The flames roared to life in an instant, searing with tremendous heat. Once they had burned everything away, they died down.

[P189]
All that remained amid the melted concrete and blackened ruins was the trace of someone who had once been there.

[P190]
And the chime of a bell that only one person in the world could hear.

[P191]
*Ding.*

[P192]
> **System**
>
> - Defeated **Lv. 153 Lee Jungryong**!
> - Gained a massive amount of **EXP**!
> - Level up!
> - Level up!

[P193]
Listening to the cheerful System notification, I slowly lowered my spear.

[P194]
*Damn old man.*

[P195]
That final smile kept coming back to me.

[P196]
What kind of life had Lee Jungryong lived? What had he been thinking at the end? And then there were those movements and his strange behavior…

[P197]
*No. I’ll think about it later.*

[P198]
The fight with Lee Jungryong had not been easy for me, either.

[P199]
Mental exhaustion suddenly washed over me, but ironically, my body felt lighter than ever thanks to the top-tier potion and the effects of leveling up.

[P200]
More than anything, I had a reason to keep moving forward.

[P201]
*The Arch Lich.*

[P202]
The source of all this.

[P203]
Before that bastard transformed this enormous city into a Gate, I had to kill—

[P204]
“H-human.”

[P205]
The Skeleton Warlord’s trembling voice reached me.

[P206]
Every hair on my body stood on end as I raised my head.

[P207]
There he was.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

# Adjudication Task — Chapter 419

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃419화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|이정룡은 문득 생각했다.
  6|
  7|‘어디서부터, 무엇이 잘못되었을까.’
  8|
  9|형님의 핏줄을 몰아내고 아레스 길드를 장악한 것?
 10|
 11|각종 불법을 저질러 끊임없이 길드를 성장시키고, 그러고도 만족하는 법 없이 욕심을 채워 나간 것?
 12|
 13|그것도 아니라면…….
 14|
 15|‘저 녀석과 적이 된 것?’
 16|
 17|이정룡의 시선이 한 사람에게 닿았다. 출혈로 인해 전신 곳곳이 피로 물들어 있는 청년.
 18|
 19|하늘을 바라보며 크게 심호흡한 그가 입술을 뗐다.
 20|
 21|“정룡아.”
 22|
 23|어째서일까. 그 나직한 목소리를 듣는 순간 이정룡은 등골이 서늘해졌다. 상처 하나 입지 않았음에도 날붙이에 베인 기분이다.
 24|
 25|그런 그를 바라보는 청년, 진태경의 입가에 광포한 웃음이 맺혔다.
 26|
 27|“발톱 자르자.”
 28|
 29|“……!”
 30|
 31|파팟!
 32|
 33|바람이 불고, 두 사람 사이에 존재하던 공간이 사라진 그 순간. 이정룡은 파공성과 함께 검을 휘둘렀다.
 34|
 35|쉬익!
 36|
 37|눈부신 기의 집약체가 진태경의 몸뚱어리를 갈랐다. 하지만 뿜어져 나와야 할 핏물 대신 바람이 흩어졌다.
 38|
 39|실체가 아닌 잔상(殘像). 이정룡의 머릿속에서 붉은색 경종이 울렸다.
 40|
 41|‘뒤!’
 42|
 43|검을 휘두르기에는 너무 늦었다. 이정룡은 번개처럼 돌아서며 주먹을 내질렀다. 새하얀 오러에 휩싸인 주먹과, 푸른 화염이 실린 손바닥이 부딪쳤다.
 44|
 45|꽈앙!
 46|
 47|세상이 뒤흔들렸다. 아니, 흔들린 것은 이정룡의 시야였다.
 48|
 49|항거할 수 없는 힘에 튕겨 나간 그가 허공에서 몸을 뒤집으며 신형을 바로잡았다.
 50|
 51|주먹이 시큰거리고 속에서 무언가가 울컥 솟구쳤다. 하지만 핏물을 뱉어 낼 틈조차 주어지지 않았다.
 52|
 53|쐐애애액!
 54|
 55|어느새 코앞까지 들이닥친 창날. 진태경이 쏘아 보낸 창이 이정룡의 가슴을 노렸다. 이를 악문 그가 온 힘을 불어넣어 검을 쳐올렸다.
 56|
 57|카가가가각! 쾅!
 58|
 59|아슬아슬하게 빗나간 창이 콘크리트를 부수며 거대한 크레이터를 남겼다.
 60|
 61|창을 흘리는 데에는 성공했지만, 가공할 만한 힘과 회전력에 찢어진 손아귀에서는 피가 튀었다.
 62|
 63|하지만 이정룡은 개의치 않고 자욱한 먼지구름 너머로 발을 뻗었다.
 64|
 65|퍼엉-!
 66|
 67|쾌속한 속도를 이기지 못한 먼지와 안개가 뿔뿔이 흩어졌다. 이정룡이 내디딘 걸음의 끝엔, 한 사람이 있었다.
 68|
 69|“저돌적인데? 내 취향이야.”
 70|
 71|어느새 새로운 창을 든 진태경이 종횡으로 창날을 내리그었다. 공간이 갈라지고 화염이 솟구쳤다. 이정룡이 내지른 검 끝은 그 중심을 정확히 꿰뚫었다.
 72|
 73|후웅, 펑!
 74|
 75|압축된 공기가 터져 나갔다. 화염이 갈라지고 새로운 길이 열렸다. 화살처럼 쏘아진 이정룡의 신형이 진태경을 향해 달려들었다.
 76|
 77|‘죽어라.’
 78|
 79|오직 한 가지 일념(一念)을 담은 검은 휘황하게 빛났고, 빛처럼 빨랐다.
 80|
 81|그러나 느려진 세상 속에서 바라본 진태경의 눈은 분명 웃고 있었다.
 82|
 83|‘이건…….’
 84|
 85|무엇인가 잘못됐다.
 86|
 87|이정룡의 생각이 미처 이어지기도 전에, 창을 쥔 진태경의 손이 흐릿해졌다.
 88|
 89|동시에 당장이라도 그의 목젖을 파고들 것 같던 검신을 후려치는 거대한 힘이 있었다.
 90|
 91|쉭! 꽈앙!
 92|
 93|귓가가 먹먹해질 만한 굉음이 울려 퍼졌다. 자의와는 상관없이 십여 미터를 미끄러진 이정룡은 치밀어 오르는 핏물을 삼켰다.
 94|

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.
